title: Do Knowledge-Rich Curriculums Cause Mental Health Problems
author: Christodoulou, Daisy
summary: Christodoulou investigates whether England's knowledge-rich education reforms have caused mental health problems in students. Using cross-UK comparisons with Scotland and Wales, which adopted different curriculum approaches, she examines wellbeing data from the WHO's Health Behaviour in School-Aged Children survey. While England's attainment rose relative to Scotland and Wales, she finds that life satisfaction declined equally across all three nations, suggesting global forces (pandemic, social media, economic insecurity) rather than curriculum type drive youth mental health trends. The data undermines claims that knowledge-rich curricula create psychological distress.
points: England's reforms produced attainment gains but mental health declined equally in Scotland and Wales, which rejected knowledge-rich approaches.
Cross-nation WHO data shows all three UK nations follow nearly identical wellbeing trends, making curriculum design an implausible sole cause.
Teen life satisfaction declined globally across Anglophone countries (US, UK, Canada, Australia), pointing to shared societal drivers, not education policy.
Journalists and policymakers conflate England with the UK, ignoring natural experiments available in Scotland and Wales.
Journalists prefer studying Helsinki than Cardiff, missing powerful counterexamples on education policy outcomes available domestically.
quotes: The timelines certainly seem to match up. England made big reforms to its education system, and mental health and social problems spiked soon after. But of course, correlation isn't causation.

The striking feature of all of this data is the similarity of the three countries' data, not the differences. Their education policies and attainment scores have definitely diverged. But happiness and wellbeing have not.
What is not plausible is to pin these dramatic UK, Anglosphere and global trends on a specific set of education policy decisions that only affected England.

For this to work journalists and policy makers in Westminster would actually have to pay attention to what is happening in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland—which by and large, they don't.” Archived from No More Marking on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
